To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The position of quantum interference (QI)-induced transmission nodes in conjugated molecules is predicted by a graphical scheme that only depends on the topology of the molecule and on the energy of the p(z) orbit of the side group.
(1) QI in molecular transport junction can be predicted solely based on molecular structure and (2) QI in aromatic molecules is more complex than in linear chains.

1) the presence of a transmission node in a conjugated molecule can be predicted from the structure alone; 2) for linear molecules the position of the node can be determined by the energy of the p(z) orbital of the side group; 3) the presence of transmission nodes in the transmission function of aromatic molecules depends on the molecular topology and the p(z) energy of the side groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic structure of organic molecules and their functionalization for applications in organic electronics.
quantum interference effects in molecular junctions.
the design of molecular devices with a controlled electronic transmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the position of transmission nodes in functional organic molecules is mainly determined by the energy of the p(z) orbital on the side group, but the presence of transmission nodes can be predicted from a diagrammatic scheme that only relies on the topology of the molecular backbone and the position of the side group.
a transmission node is likely to appear in a molecular junction if there is a functional group with a p(z) energy close to the Fermi energy.
the position of the QI induced transmission node in a molecular junction is a function of the side group p(z) energy and the position of the side group with respect to the molecular backbone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an intuitive graphical method for predicting the nodal structure of transmission functions of molecular junctions.
the nodal structure of the transmission function can be understood in terms of the molecular graph.
QI in molecular transport junction is a general phenomenon that can be predicted from the molecular structure alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nodal structure of the transmission function of a molecular transport junction can be predicted by inspection of a simple diagrammatic representation of the molecular structure.
the graphical method can be used to qualitatively predict QI in molecular transport junction, which can help to identify promising molecules for molecular electronics applications.
the presence and position of transmission nodes in conjugated molecular junctions can be predicted from simple molecular graphs.
